verdict:
REVIEWED BY cc 2026-10-06. ELIGIBILITY FIRST, because this record names the reviewer by role rather than by agent: I am a build session, I am not the author (hover2), I hold no claim on .claude/skills/sairn-hover-auditor/ -- `sairn_claim.py list` at HEAD shows two active claims, hank's on platform files and fourth's on exec-context/methodology, neither touching that path -- and I am not either hover instance. Eligible.

THE RECORD REFUSES "reviewed, no findings" UNLESS IT NAMES WHAT WAS OPENED AND WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR, so both are listed in full.

WHAT I OPENED
  - .claude/skills/sairn-hover-auditor/tools-hover2/stale_basis_check.py -- 9,589 bytes, 226 lines -- READ ONLY, and parsed with `ast` rather than EXECUTED. Running an auditor tool from a build clone would itself be the boundary this obligation is partly about, so the whole review is static.
  - tools/tier_a_review_gate.py, tests/run_tier_a_review_gate_probe.py and docs/tier-a-reviews.json, read to decide whether anything invokes the subject.
  - Nothing under .claude/skills/sairn-hover-auditor/ was opened for writing, no gate there was armed, and no file there was modified.

WHAT I LOOKED FOR
  - Every `open()` / `io.open()` call, with its MODE resolved from the AST rather than grepped, and every filesystem-mutating or process-spawning call (os.remove, os.unlink, os.rmdir, os.replace, os.rename, os.makedirs, os.mkdir, shutil.rmtree/copy/move, system, run, Popen, check_output, call, exec, eval, __import__).
  - Every line containing the string "quotes", case-insensitive.
  - Word-bounded transport tokens that could reach a resource: rest(, fetch(, urlopen, requests., supabase, postgrest, POST, PATCH.
  - Every `sys.exit()` argument.
  - `git grep -l stale_basis_check` across the whole repo, and then for each file found, whether any NON-COMMENT line actually invokes or imports it.
  - Literal platform paths named in the source.

WHAT I FOUND -- the three questions the record asks, answered by measurement

(1) IS IT READ-ONLY TOWARD PLATFORM DATA? YES. Three `open()` calls, all mode 'r' (paths computed, so the literal is not in the AST); ZERO write-mode opens; ZERO calls to any of the twelve mutating or spawning functions listed above. The only platform document it names is docs/CRITICALITY-TIERS.md, which is the register it exists to read.

(2) DOES IT CONSTRUCT A WRITE TO `quotes`? NO, and the resource is not involved at all. The string "quotes" appears on exactly TWO lines, both of them prose: `:48` "straight or markdown-emphasised quotes, or introduced by a past-tense" -- the plain English noun, about quotation marks -- and `:185` inside a test label, "a row that QUOTES the boilerplate while explaining". Neither is the `quotes` resource. The tool constructs no transport of any kind, so it cannot write to that resource or to any other.

(3) IS IT REPORT-ONLY? YES, and more strongly than report-only: it is UNWIRED. Three files name the string and NONE invokes it -- all three mentions are prose about this very obligation ("`quotes` in stale_basis_check.py's prose (seq 422)"). No hook, push gate or test runs it.

SO THE `quotes` ATTRIBUTION IS A FALSE POSITIVE, and that is now mechanically supportable rather than argued. I fixed strip_diff_noise() in fa2aebf7 so prose COMMENT bodies are blanked before the resource match; line 48 is a full-line `#` comment of more than three words and is exactly the shape that fix blanks. Line 185 is a prose string of more than three words and was already blanked by the pre-existing rule. This obligation is therefore one of the instances in open-work row 95, and the record's own derivation -- recomputing the resource list at HEAD with the gate's own tier_a_resources() and touched_tier_a() rather than copying it -- was the right method and reached the right answer.

TWO FINDINGS AGAINST MY OWN REVIEW, recorded because they are the same defect class as the obligation itself and I would rather they be in the record than not:
  - My transport check tested `'st(' in src` and it MATCHED, twice, inside `selftest(`. That is the substring defect this platform records as `esign` matching 47 occurrences of `design`. Word-bounded now, and `st(` dropped entirely: the st() storage helper is browser-side and cannot appear in a Python tool, so including it could only ever manufacture a false positive.
  - My caller check treated every file naming the string as a build-side caller, and reported three. All three name it in a COMMENT about this obligation. Fixed to test for an invocation shape on a non-comment line. I committed the fix for exactly this distinction in the Tier A gate one commit earlier and then repeated the mistake in my own probe within the hour, which is worth recording as evidence that the pattern is not obvious even to somebody who has just fixed it.

ON THE PROCESS FINDING THE RECORD RAISES, which I think is the sharpest thing in it and is not about this tool: the push of e3758d37 was PERMITTED by an obligation record that was written to disk and then reset from the working tree, because tools/hover_auditor_scope_gate.py refuses that path from the auditor's clone. A gate satisfied by something that did not persist is worse than either outcome alone, and the retrospective record is the right repair. It is not closed by this review -- the structural question is how the auditor opens an obligation at all when the only register is in a path its own scope gate forbids it to write, and that needs a decision from whoever owns the separation enforcement rather than a verdict from me. CONFIRMED AS OPEN, naming it rather than letting the retrospective record stand as if the mechanism were fixed.

VERDICT: sound. Report-only, read-only toward platform data, unwired, constructs no transport, and the `quotes` attribution is a false positive confirmed by measurement rather than assertion. 12 arms, exit 0, after two corrections to my own probe.
